ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $ \triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF$. If $AC = 5$ and $CF = 2$, what is the length of $CD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\triangle ABC\cong \triangle DEF$, $\angle A$ and $\angle D$ are corresponding angles, and $AB$ and $DE$ are corresponding sides,\\
$\therefore AC=DF=5$,\\
Also, since $CF=2$,\\
$\therefore CD=DF-CF=5-2=\boxed{3}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF$. If $AC = 5$ and $CF = 2$, what is the length of $CD$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are two triangles in the figure; points A, F, C, D are on the same straight line slanting downward to the right, and C is between F and D; triangle ABC is on the upper left, and triangle DEF is on the lower right. Reasoning: From the corresponding order of triangle ABC congruent to triangle DEF, it can be known that A corresponds to D, B corresponds to E, and C corresponds to F, so side AC corresponds to side DF. Therefore DF = AC = 5. Because C is between F and D, DF = CF + CD. It is known that CF = 2, therefore CD = 5 - 2 = 3.
